title: Candidate admission, diversity, ordering and display
purpose: Identify precisely where good candidates disappear and weak or repeated candidates enter or dominate the slate.

executionReceipt.executionModeEvidence: Runtime reports session origin 'desktop_app'. No Claude CLI subprocess was invoked; policy assigns Job 6 to Desktop directly.
executionReceipt.modelMetadataSource: claude-code-remote get_session, read in Job 1 of this session
recordedCaveats: EXECUTION_POLICY.json sets recordResolvedModel=true for this job and names no required model, so none was applied or assumed.
Job 1's caveat stands: the surface is Claude Desktop with origin 'desktop_app', but execution is cloud-backed.
Fable 5.1 was not used and must not be for this job.

evidenceBasis.primaryOracle: The attributed editor review artifacts, reviewer dwaynetoler: reports/storypackage-02-future-volksgeist-v12-candidate-review.json with 48 decisions over 47 tasks, and reports/storypackage-02-jayz-drake-settle-it-v13-candidate-review.json with 12 decisions over 12 tasks. Job 1 hash-verified both against the evidence package.
evidenceBasis.whyThisOracle: These decisions are keyed taskId::candidateId and carry the editor's own words, so a complaint can be joined to the exact candidate and task. They are ATTRIBUTED, unlike the 49 matching_output_feedback records that Job 3 correction C-5 established carry packageId null (UE-22). Job 6 therefore rests on the attributed set and does not use the unattributed corpus as an oracle.
evidenceBasis.statusVersusComment: Status and comment are separate authorities and are not conflated. Future statuses are rejected 3, acceptable 11, unreviewed 34; Jay-Z are acceptable 2, unreviewed 10. Many unreviewed rows carry a substantive comment, including 'All acceptable selections', so unreviewed is a workflow state and NOT a rejection. Sentiment is read from the comment text only.

lineageCompleteness.limitation: 21 of the 47 reviewed future-volksgeist tasks have no focused-diversity record, so for those the admitted, hidden and not-admitted family sets are unknown and their findings are typed lineage_incomplete rather than guessed.

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: Retrieval and eligibility
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.implementation: media_candidates.py eligible pool; eligibility-overrides.json; binding scope field
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: Pool filter before capability reasoning; dated attributed overrides are the right mechanism.

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: Structured capability admission
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: Generous. 4896 candidate cards over 310 future-volksgeist tasks, 310 of 310 with at least one candidate. Median admitted families 61 (future-volksgeist) and 41 (jayz-drake).
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.observedLoss: Across the 38 tasks with COMPLETE lineage, not one editor-requested family class fell in notAdmittedCatalogFamilies.
failureTypes: admission_error (0 evidenced, scoped to the 38 complete tasks)

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: Feasibility and native fit
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: conditional 40, incompatible 1, zero native_fit on the 41-task Year Seventeen run.
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.observedLoss: feasibility_unknown is the normal state by design.
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.scope: measured on the Year Seventeen corpus only

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: B-roll and no-template routing
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: NO ROUTE EVIDENCE EXISTS FOR THE REVIEWED TASKS. ordered-visual-route-plan.json holds 41 scenes, all of them grammar/visual-tasks.json ids (Year Seventeen), with 32 template_review and 9 broll. It covers 0 of 59 reviewed tasks.
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.observedLoss: Undetermined for the reviewed set. 16 reviewed tasks carry an editor b-roll request and none has an observed route. Template candidates WERE still displayed on all 16, each with a gallery slate.
failureTypes: forced_template (UNDETERMINED for the reviewed set; not evidenced either way)

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: Family ordering
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: Two ordering halves with different signals. Displayed exposures on jayz-drake p04-4-03 span 3 to 136, so the first eight are diversify-ranked and the second eight are low-exposure exploration.
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.observedLoss: ordering_loss. The pie family ranked outside both halves: exposure 24 slates, 27th of 41 by ascending exposure, against twelve admitted families at zero exposure.

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: Variant ordering within a family
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: A real eight-key ranking: (picked, enc, fit, clear, declared, rel, still, id). Only id is arbitrary and the docstring says so. FAM_MAX=1 is an intentional review-budget policy.
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.observedLoss: variant_collapse, but only where a materially better variant existed. Proven on future-volksgeist p03-2-01.
failureTypes: variant_collapse (proven on the named cases, not on every one-variant slate)

stagesEvaluatedSeparately.name: Display cap and focused-review sampling
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.finding: Uniform: 16 and 6 on every focused task in both packages, with no stated derivation.
stagesEvaluatedSeparately.observedLoss: 2210 hidden admitted family appearances across 59 focused tasks. The cap ENFORCES what ordering already decided; it is the first divergence only where ordering placed a family inside a surviving half and the cap still cut it, which was not observed.
failureTypes: display_loss (0 evidenced as a FIRST divergence; systemic in magnitude)

failureTypeDefinitions.not_in_catalog: no catalog family can serve the requested class
failureTypeDefinitions.metadata_gap: the family exists and its capability record cannot express what the task needs
failureTypeDefinitions.contract_gap: the task never carried the information needed to request the right family
failureTypeDefinitions.admission_error: a catalog family that could serve the request was not admitted
failureTypeDefinitions.feasibility_unknown: fit could not be established, so the candidate reaches the editor undetermined
failureTypeDefinitions.ordering_loss: a family was admitted and the ordering strategy placed it outside every surviving slot; the first divergence is ordering even though a cap enforced it
failureTypeDefinitions.display_loss: ordering placed a family inside a surviving slot and the cap removed it anyway; non-overlapping with ordering_loss
failureTypeDefinitions.family_duplication: one family recurs across slates so that the slate reads as repetitive
failureTypeDefinitions.forced_template: a template route was proposed where no template was the right answer
failureTypeDefinitions.variant_collapse: the right family reached the editor and a materially better variant existed that the system could not expose. Proven only where both hold; a one-variant-per-family slate alone is an intentional review-budget policy, not a failure
failureTypeDefinitions.displayed_but_rejected: DEFINED BY THIS JOB for honesty. The requested family class WAS displayed and the editor still judged the slate inadequate. This is not a retrieval, admission, ordering or display failure and must not be counted as one.
failureTypeDefinitions.valid_no_template_outcome: the editor names b-roll or no template as correct; a right answer, not a failure
failureTypeDefinitions.lineage_incomplete: the task has no focused-diversity record, so admitted and hidden sets are unknown
failureTypeDefinitions.sibling_propagation_loss: _siblings is computed by the variant ranker and dropped by template_candidates() before publication, so the ranked alternatives reach no artifact or review surface

primaryFinding.statement: The variant ranker works and the review-budget cap is deliberate. The defect is that the sibling list built to make that cap recoverable is dropped one function before publication.
proof: _within_family ranks on eight keys; only the last is arbitrary and the docstring names it.
match-trial/candidates.py:800 computes r["_siblings"] as the rest of the ranked family.
_siblings appears in no file under reports/.
The code comment at match-trial/candidates.py:795-799 already records 429 hidden siblings across 40 beats and that the editor raised "right family, wrong scene" twice.

provenDisplayLoss.editorQuote: this first part of this beat calls for a pie chart to show porportion. none are good for that.
provenDisplayLoss.verifiedLineage: The catalog holds exactly one pie family, 3d-pie-chart-set. On this task it is in hiddenAdmittedFamilies: admitted by the capability pass, then withheld by the 16-family display limit. It is absent from displayedFamilies and from the gallery slate.
provenDisplayLoss.reading: A fully closed loop: the editor asked for a pie chart, the catalog has one, admission admitted it, and the display cap hid it. This is display_loss proven end to end against an attributed editor request, and it is the cleanest instance in the corpus.

whatIsNotTheProblem.basis: _within_family ranks on eight keys; only the final id tiebreak is arbitrary and the code says so.

whatIsNotTheProblem.claim: one variant per family is itself a failure
whatIsNotTheProblem.basis: FAM_MAX=1 is an intentional review-budget policy with a stated reason in the code.
the pie-chart case is ordering_loss; the cap only enforced what ordering decided.
no reviewed task has an observed route; the route artifact covers Year Seventeen only.

whatIsNotTheProblem.claim: good candidates are filtered out by admission
whatIsNotTheProblem.basis: holds across the 38 tasks with complete lineage; the 21 incomplete tasks are excluded.

whatIsNotTheProblem.claim: the slate is dominated by repeated families
whatIsNotTheProblem.basis: 4 of 59 tasks flag recurrence; dedup is total within a slate and variety rises 58 to 94.

retrievalAdmissionOrderingDisplayNeverCo.verdict: SATISFIED, AND EVIDENCED BY FOUR SEPARATE BOUNDARY STATEMENTS IN THE ARTIFACTS
evidence: diversity boundary = 'An admitted family is eligible for editor review only; this report does not establish native fit.'
_presentation_candidates returns an evidenceBoundary of 'retrieval_is_candidate_discovery; fit_is_exact_evidence_comparison; neither_is_selection'
retrievalAdmissionOrderingDisplayNeverCo.auditDiscipline: This job reports each of the seven stages separately with its own measured loss and never aggregates them into a single score or rate.

historicalEditorChoiceDoesNotAdmit.verdict: SATISFIED FOR ADMISSION, WITH AN ORDERING INFLUENCE NOW STATED
admissionEvidence: visualtask_matching admits only from the structured capability record and has no prior-choice reference.
carry_prior_route_choices acts only on rows already at template_review and adds no candidate.
historicalEditorChoiceDoesNotAdmit.orderingInfluenceFound: _within_family's first and strongest sort key is "picked = honor_global_picks and r[id] not in _picked_ids()", so a previously selected record sorts FIRST within its family, and visualtask_matching.py:311 passes honor_global_picks=not task.get("ignorePriorSelections", False), on by default.
historicalEditorChoiceDoesNotAdmit.reading: Prior editor choice does not ADMIT a candidate, which is what the acceptance check asks, but it does ORDER one. The published basis implied no influence anywhere; that is corrected here (C6-5). The task-level override ignorePriorSelections exists and is surfaced as ignoredPriorStorySelections in the candidate provenance.

noTemplateRemainsValid.verdict: SATISFIED AS AN AUDIT DISCIPLINE; NOT VERIFIED AS A ROUTE OUTCOME
noTemplateRemainsValid.auditDiscipline: 16 reviewed tasks carry an editor b-roll request, typed valid_no_template_outcome and excluded from failure counts by definition. No finding in this job treats the absence of a template as a defect.
noTemplateRemainsValid.routeOutcomeNotVerified: Whether those 16 were actually routed to b-roll is undetermined: no reviewed task appears in the route plan (UE-36). The published claim rested on a global fallback flag and a miscounted route total.

noCodeChanges.evidence: All analysis ran read-only from committed artifacts and read-only module inspection. Only the two Job 6 report files were created.

unresolvedEvidence.item: No reviewed task has an observed route. ordered-visual-route-plan.json covers only the 41 Year Seventeen tasks, so b-roll and no-template routing is unverified for all 59 reviewed tasks and for the 16 where the editor asked for it.

_encfit, _capfit and _rel are annotated during a live retrieval run and recorded in no committed artifact, so the ranked order of variants within a family cannot be replayed from the pinned inputs. The displayed variant, the existence of better variants, and the severing of _siblings are all established without them.

match-trial/candidates.py is load-bearing for diversification and variant ranking yet appears nowhere in REFERENCE_MANIFEST.md's declared transformation path, which is why Job 6 first missed it. The manifest understates the audited surface.
displayLimit 16 and slideshowLimit 6 are uniform with no stated derivation.
Focused review covers 26/310 and 33/186 tasks; the sampling rationale is not reconstructable.
21 of 47 reviewed future-volksgeist tasks have no committed lineage and could not be reconstructed.
Whether the review surface shows the variant id cannot be established here, and it now matters more: _siblings never reaches the surface either way.
Mixed-payload handling has no consumer; no split route is produced in any artifact.

acceptance.check: Retrieval, admission, ordering and display are never collapsed into one score
acceptance.basis: Now seven separate lineage stages, with family ordering (5) and variant ordering (6) split out from the display cap (7), and ordering_loss and display_loss defined as non-overlapping first divergences. Five boundary statements are still quoted from the artifacts. No stage is aggregated into a score.

acceptance.check: Historical editor choice does not admit a new-story candidate
acceptance.basis: Verified at three sites for ADMISSION, and the correction adds the ordering influence the published version implied away: prior picks are the first sort key inside a family, on by default. Admission is unaffected, which is what the check asks; the distinction is now stated rather than elided.

acceptance.check: No template remains a valid correct outcome
acceptance.verdict: PASS as audit discipline, with the route outcome explicitly unverified
acceptance.basis: 16 b-roll requests are typed valid_no_template_outcome and excluded from failure counts; nothing treats a missing template as a defect. The separate claim that routing handled them correctly is WITHDRAWN, because no reviewed task has an observed route (UE-36).
Read-only throughout, including the newly opened match-trial/candidates.py. The diff touches only the two Job 6 artifacts and the canonical correction file.

result_detail.headline: Corrected. The variant ranker works, the display cap is deliberate, and the real defect is a severed sibling list. Ordering, not the cap, is where the pie chart was lost.
result_detail.oneLine: _within_family ranks variants on eight keys and builds _siblings so the editor can reach the rest of the family; template_candidates() drops it before publication, so it reaches no artifact - and the code comment already recorded 429 hidden siblings and the editor saying "right family, wrong scene" twice.

reviewedTaskLineage.requirement: For every reviewed task used, the complete candidate lineage with editor response.

correctionRequest.accepted: in full; all four items were correct, and item 2 pointed at a module this job never opened

corrections.request: Ordering loss was declared zero merely because display cuts by a fixed count rather than a scalar score.
corrections.action: Accepted and reclassified. The 16-family cut is applied AFTER an explicit ordering strategy, eight_primary_plus_eight_least_exposed_admitted_families, and that ordering decides which admitted families survive. Traced for the pie-chart case on jayz-drake p04-4-03: 41 families admitted, 16 displayed, 25 hidden. 3d-pie-chart-set has an exposure of 24 slates and ranks 27th of 41 by ascending exposure, while twelve admitted families had ZERO exposure, so it was nowhere near the least-exposed half; and it did not rank in the eight primary diversify-ranked slots. The displayed sixteen span exposures 3 to 136, confirming the two halves have different ordering signals. It therefore became unavailable at ORDERING, not at the cap: had either half ranked it, the same 16-family cap would have kept it. The case is reclassified from display_loss to ordering_loss, and the two are now defined as non-overlapping first divergences.

corrections.request: The variant-selection mechanism was described as arbitrary with no way to choose the right variant; C.diversify ranks variants and computes _siblings, which template_candidates omits.
corrections.action: Accepted; the published description was wrong and the request named code this job never opened. The ranking lives in match-trial/candidates.py, reached through visualtask_matching.py:18 "import candidates as C" after sys.path.insert of ROOT/match-trial, and called at visualtask_matching.py:304 as C.diversify(...). _within_family (match-trial/candidates.py:682) returns an eight-key sort tuple: (picked, enc, fit, clear, declared, rel, still, id) - prior user pick, encoding fit, declared capacity fit, binding verdict clear over conditional, declared subject capacity, negated relevance, clip over still, then id. Only the LAST key is arbitrary and the docstring names it as such, so "arbitrary representative" is withdrawn. FAM_MAX=1 showing one representative per family is an intentional review-budget policy with a stated reason, so a one-variant-per-family slate is NOT by itself a failure. The real defect is narrower and is proven below.

corrections.request: Lineage coverage: 59 tasks used but 21 lack admitted/hidden sets while only one finding was typed lineage_incomplete, obscuring the task-level gap.
corrections.action: Accepted. The two counts are now reported separately and never substituted for one another: 59 reviewed tasks, 38 with COMPLETE committed lineage, 21 INCOMPLETE tasks, against 1 lineage_incomplete FINDING. Reconstruction was attempted and is not available from committed artifacts: all 21 have a post-cut gallery slate, but 0 of 21 carry admittedFamilyCount or hiddenAdmittedFamilies, and the pre-cut admitted set requires re-running admission with exhaustive_families=True, which no committed artifact records for these tasks. They are therefore marked incomplete and excluded from every conclusion requiring admission, hidden-family or first-divergence evidence. Verified that this exclusion changes no classification: zero findings on those 21 tasks rested on admitted, hidden or ordering evidence.

corrections.request: B-roll routing was concluded from a global fallback flag and a route count, not from the actual route of the 16 reviewed tasks where the editor asked for b-roll.
corrections.action: Accepted, and this exposed the most serious error in the published job. reports/ordered-visual-route-plan.json holds 41 scenes whose taskIds are all 41 ids of grammar/visual-tasks.json - the Year Seventeen corpus - and it covers 0 of the 59 reviewed future-volksgeist and jayz-drake tasks. So NONE of the 16 b-roll-request tasks has any observed route outcome at this baseline. The published route counts were also wrong: they were collected by globbing reports/*route*.json and double-counted; the plan actually holds 32 template_review and 9 broll, not 64 and 18. The conclusion that forced_template is unsupported is WITHDRAWN for the reviewed set and re-scoped to the Year Seventeen corpus, which is the only corpus with route evidence. Recorded unresolved as UE-36.

corrections.request: Not raised by the request; found while verifying item 2.
corrections.action: The published acceptance basis for "historical editor choice does not admit a new-story candidate" was correct about ADMISSION but overstated. _within_family's first and strongest sort key is "picked = honor_global_picks and r[id] not in _picked_ids()", so a previously selected record sorts FIRST within its family, and visualtask_matching.py:311 passes honor_global_picks=not task.get("ignorePriorSelections", False), i.e. ON by default. Prior editor choice does not ADMIT a candidate, which the acceptance check asks, but it does ORDER one. The acceptance basis is rewritten to state that distinction explicitly rather than implying prior choice has no influence anywhere.

orderingVersusDisplay.rule: ordering_loss and display_loss are non-overlapping first divergences. ordering_loss is assigned when a family was admitted and the ordering strategy placed it outside every surviving slot. display_loss is assigned only when ordering placed a family inside a surviving slot and the cap removed it anyway.

theCodeAlreadyDiagnosedThis.quote: FAM_MAX=1 was set after a slate came back 7 scenes from one pack - the cap is right, but it hides 429 bound siblings across 40 beats and the user has twice said "right family, wrong scene" with no way to reach the sibling.
theCodeAlreadyDiagnosedThis.reading: The codebase names the exact defect this job rediscovered, quantifies it at 429 hidden siblings across 40 beats, and records that the editor raised it twice. The audit adds the downstream reason it still bites.

theProvenDefect.statement: _siblings is computed and then dropped before publication. visualtask_matching.template_candidates() returns a row containing only candidateId, name, condition, bindingProvenance and candidateMatchingProvenance, so _siblings is not in the returned dict.
theProvenDefect.verified: grep for _siblings across every file in reports/ returns nothing: it reaches no gallery, no diversity artifact, no review queue and therefore no review surface.
theProvenDefect.consequence: The escape hatch the code built for exactly this complaint is severed one function before it would be published. The editor cannot reach the sibling because the sibling list never leaves the matcher.
theProvenDefect.firstDivergentStage: variant ordering output, not variant ranking

provenCase.editorRequest: intro-slideshow-full-720p--scene-012 is a good selection as well but shouldve shown the version with 2-3 cards, not 6 ... 2 slots would be prefered
provenCase.whyThisMeetsTheBar: A materially better variant demonstrably existed - the editor asked for 2 to 3 slots and the family contains both 3-slot sequences and 1-at-once/2-total sequences - and the system could not EXPOSE it, because _siblings carrying the other 37 is dropped at the return.
provenCase.orderingKeysCaveat: The exact per-variant key values (_encfit, _capfit, _rel) are annotated upstream during a live retrieval run and are not recorded in any committed artifact, so the ranked order of the 38 variants for this task cannot be replayed from the pinned inputs. What IS established from the committed data: the displayed variant, the existence of better-fitting variants, and the severing of _siblings. Recorded as UE-37.

variantCollapseRevised.notAFailure: A one-variant-per-family slate is not by itself a failure. FAM_MAX=1 is a deliberate review-budget policy. The failure is the dropped sibling list, which is what makes the policy unrecoverable for the editor.
